findings.title: Step 5b's boot-log example names four wrong JSON fields, so the new flag-flip verification procedure cannot be followed
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The example prints {"level":"info","prefix":"[worker]","msg":"Feature flags","flags":{…}}. The emitter is logBootFlagSummary (worker/boot-flag-summary.ts:94) -> logger.log('Feature flags', { flags: buildBootFlagSummary() }), and createWorkerLogger assembles the record in src/lib/shared/logger.ts: buildBaseRecord (:57-68) writes timestamp, level, service, logger: normalizeLoggerName(prefix), message; emit (:158-175) attaches the object arg as record.data. The real line is {"timestamp":…,"level":"info","service":"worker","logger":"worker","message":"Feature flags","data":{"flags":{…}}}. Wrong: prefix->logger, "[worker]"->"worker" (normalizeLoggerName, logger.ts:29-31, strips the brackets — the same equivalence round 1 established under RT-13), msg->message, and flags is nested under data. P0 rather than P1 because step 5b closes with an operational instruction keyed to what the operator sees — 'A logged value that disagrees with what you set means the restart has not landed: wait for it, do not set it again' — so an operator searching on "prefix":"[worker]" or a top-level flags key finds nothing and the procedure tells them to keep waiting. The rest of 5b is true: thirteen booleans keyed by env var name including all six autonomy flags, and the provenance claim resolves at docs/runbooks/evidence/2026-09-07-staging-triage-flag-flip.md:60.

findings.title: The std-M3 suppression makes the settings page render the green 'You can widen or narrow auto-posting whenever you like' while the server says canExpand: false
findings.arbiter_reasoning: readinessCopy drops auto_approval_disabled and provider_moderation_disabled whenever state.data.posting.blocked is true (:266-273), but the blocked banner that restates them renders only when !account.suspended && posting.blocked && (account.threshold !== null || overrideNames.length > 0) (:711-716). In the gap the reason is suppressed and nothing says it — and an empty list is not silent: ReadinessBlock (:1403-1410) renders '✓ You can widen or narrow auto-posting whenever you like' when items.length === 0, while canExpand is computed server-side from the UNFILTERED list (src/lib/auto-approval/readiness.ts:45). MEASURED by differential probe, applied as a journaled mutation of AutoApprovalClient.test.tsx and run at both SHAs. Probe A (account default off, no overrides, readiness.blockReasons = ['provider_moderation_disabled'], canExpand false, posting.blocked true): PASSES at HEAD 9a7a459f9 — 'Off. You approve every reply before it posts.', moderation sentence absent, green affirmative present; FAILS at 825f0fbbf — 'Safety screening for replies is switched off right now, so auto-posting cannot be widened.' is on screen. Probe B (same flags, suspended, threshold 4): same result. Reachability: OPENAI_MODERATION_ENABLED=false produces exactly this pair — buildAutoApprovalPostingStatus (posting-status.ts:59) and buildAutoApprovalReadiness (readiness.ts:34) push the same name, which is why the pair was chosen for the suppression set. auto_approval_disabled cannot be the sole suppressed reason (with the runtime off, autopilotAvailable at settings.ts:1196-1199 is false too), but provider_moderation_disabled alone is reachable. Probe B widens a pre-existing policy_suspended hole; probe A is new in this pass. The fix is also untested: deleting the filter line leaves the suite at 58/58, and the nearest covering candidate (:413-428) inherits posting.blocked: false from baseState — a state the server cannot produce.

findings.title: The go-live-derived oracle reads exactly one line of flag-flip/SKILL.md, so a flag added on a wrapped line passes silently
findings.arbiter_reasoning: skill.split('\n').find(line => line.includes('The go-live order is fixed')) takes a single line and matches /`([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)`/g in it. Today .claude/skills/flag-flip/SKILL.md:17 holds all six names on one line and the test correctly kills a dropped key (measured: removing AUTOPILOT_PURCHASABLE fails 7 titles, this one among them). A seventh flag appended on a wrapped continuation line, or written without backticks, is silently not checked — the exact failure mode the test exists to prevent. Rewording 'The go-live order is fixed' breaks it, but deliberately and with a legible message, which is a reasonable tripwire rather than a spurious break.
